defs: Short videos or pictures that try to sell things
Things on TV that make you want to buy
Messages that tell you about things to buy
exs: I saw funny ads on TV about toys.
There are many ads in the magazine.
We skip the ads before the video starts.

defs: A small thing you push to make something work
You push it to turn a machine on
A small part you press to start a game
exs: Carlos pushed the red button on the robot.
Push the button to turn on the light.
Which button do I push to start the game?

defs: A small machine made to do one job
A tool like a phone or a clock
A small machine that uses power to help us
exs: This new device can wash dishes.
Mom's phone is a very useful device.
Dad bought a small device to clean the floor.

defs: Money that people use in America
A bill or coin used to buy things
One hundred cents make one of these
exs: The pencil costs one dollar.
Carlos found a dollar on the street.
She paid a dollar for the lemonade.

defs: A hard, shiny material like iron
A strong material that robots are made of
A hard material that feels cold
exs: The robot was made of metal.
A metal spoon felt cold in my hand.
I dropped a metal spoon on the floor.

defs: Short parts of time; sixty make an hour
Units we use to count a short time
Small parts of an hour
exs: The bus will come in five minutes.
Carlos read for twenty minutes.
Wait a few minutes, then come back.

defs: To see something and know it is there
To see a small thing that is easy to miss
To look and see what is around you
exs: Did you notice the new robot?
Carlos did not notice the mud on his shoes.
I did not notice the bird in the tree.

defs: A room where people work at desks
A place with desks, computers and phones for work
A room where a boss or a teacher works
exs: Dad works in a big office in the city.
The teachers' office is down the hall.
Carlos went to the office to see his teacher.

defs: A machine that can move and do jobs
A metal helper that a computer controls
A machine that looks a bit like a person
exs: The robot picked up the box.
Carlos built a small robot at school.
The robot said hello in a funny voice.

defs: Having a shiny gray-white color
The shiny color of some coins and spoons
The color of the moon at night
exs: The robot had a silver face.
She wore a silver ring on her finger.
The moon looked silver in the sky.

defs: A room where things are kept until needed
A place at school for extra things
A small room full of boxes
exs: The mops are in the storeroom.
Carlos found an old robot in the storeroom.
The storeroom was dark and dirty.

defs: To walk around slowly with no plan
To go from place to place for fun
To walk away without a goal
exs: Mosh likes to wander around the garden.
Don't wander off in the busy market.
We wander along the beach every summer.

defs: To say that you did something wrong
To say the truth about a mistake
To tell people you made a mistake
exs: Carlos had to admit he broke the lamp.
I admit I was afraid of the dark.
She did not want to admit she was wrong.

defs: Covered with small bits of dry dirt
Not clean because nobody wiped it
Full of dirt that sits on things
exs: The old books were dusty.
Carlos sneezed in the dusty room.
A dusty road led to the farm.

defs: Very happy about something that will happen
Full of joy and ready for fun
Happy and unable to wait
exs: Carlos was excited about the trip.
The kids were excited to see the snow.
Mosh jumped up, excited to play.

defs: To take something quickly with your hand
To pick something up in a hurry
To hold something suddenly and tightly
exs: Grab your coat and let's go!
Carlos had to grab the rope.
I will grab a snack before school.

defs: Said unhappy words in a low voice
Talked in a cross way about something
Spoke in a low, unhappy voice
exs: Carlos grumbled about his homework.
She grumbled when it started to rain.
Grandpa grumbled that the soup was cold.

defs: A part cut or broken from something
One bit of a bigger thing
One part of a cake or puzzle
exs: I ate a piece of cake.
Carlos lost one piece of the puzzle.
Mom handed me a piece of paper.

defs: Shut something with a loud bang
Closed a door very hard and fast
Pushed a door shut with a big noise
exs: Carlos slammed the door by accident.
The wind slammed the window shut.
He slammed the door and ran outside.

defs: Something you put in a toy to give power
A small thing that keeps power for a phone
A part that gives a clock power to run
exs: The robot needs a new battery.
My flashlight has a weak battery.
Carlos changed the battery in the clock.

defs: A short road from the street to a house
The place beside a house where cars park
A path where you park near the garage
exs: Dad parked the car in the driveway.
Carlos cleaned snow off the driveway.
We played ball in the driveway.

defs: Very worried and rushing around because of fear
Unable to stay calm because you are scared
Hurrying around in a nervous, upset way
exs: Carlos made a frantic search for his lost key.
The frantic puppy ran in circles in the storm.
Mom became frantic when she could not find the baby.

defs: To stop moving or stop what you do
To come to a stop right now
To stand still and not go on
exs: The robot had to halt when its battery ran out.
The teacher told the class to halt at the door.
Please halt your bike before you cross the road.

defs: A light in a case that you carry
A lamp with a handle that you take camping
A light used outside when it is dark
exs: Carlos hung a lantern outside the tent at night.
We carried a lantern down the dark path.
The lantern lit up the whole cave.

defs: A person who lives next to your house
Someone who lives close to you
A person who lives on your street
exs: Our neighbor waters his flowers every morning.
Carlos waved at his neighbor over the fence.
The friendly neighbor gave us fresh apples.

defs: A slippery liquid that helps machines move well
A liquid you put on squeaky parts
A thick liquid that stops parts from squeaking
exs: The robot's arm needed a drop of oil.
Dad put oil on the squeaky door.
The old bike needs some oil.

defs: To push down on something with your finger
To push a button to make it work
To push hard on something with your hand
exs: Carlos will press the red button to start the robot.
Please press the doorbell twice.
Press here to open the box.

defs: A big piece of schoolwork done over time
Work like building a model for school
A school job you plan and finish
exs: Carlos built a robot for his science project.
Our class project is about frogs.
She worked hard on her art project.

defs: To stop doing something and give up
To stop trying before you finish
To leave something and not come back
exs: Carlos did not quit when the robot fell down.
I will never quit practicing my violin.
He wanted to quit the game because he was tired.

defs: To take something away from a place
To take something off
To get something out of a place
exs: Please remove your muddy shoes at the door.
Carlos had to remove the robot's broken arm.
Can you remove the lid from the jar?

defs: A plant with thorns and pretty flowers
A garden plant that grows red or pink flowers
A small bush in a garden with sweet flowers
exs: Mosh hid behind the rosebush in the garden.
A bee buzzed around the red rosebush.
Grandma planted a new rosebush by the gate.

defs: A set of questions to see what you know
Something you do at school to check learning
Questions you answer to show what you learned
exs: We have a spelling test on Friday.
Carlos did well on his math test.
I studied hard for my English test.

defs: A thin metal string that carries electricity
A long thin metal thread you can bend
A thin metal cord used to join things
exs: Carlos used a wire to join the robot's parts.
Don't touch the loose wire on the lamp.
The bird sat on the wire outside my window.

defs: To think that something is true
To be sure someone tells the truth
To think that something is real
exs: I believe Mosh can learn a new trick.
Do you believe in magic?
Carlos could not believe his eyes when the robot danced.

defs: Small jobs you do around the house
Daily work like washing dishes
Jobs that help keep a home clean
exs: Carlos finished his chores before playing outside.
Washing dishes is one of my chores.
My brother and I share the chores at home.

defs: To run very fast for a short time
To rush somewhere very fast
To hurry off in a quick run
exs: Carlos had to dash to catch the bus.
The rabbit will dash across the field.
I saw Mosh dash out of the door.

defs: Showed how to do something to others
Showed people how something works
Let people watch how a thing is done
exs: The robot demonstrated how to sweep the floor.
Our teacher demonstrated the science trick.
Carlos demonstrated his new skateboard move.

defs: With nothing inside it
Not holding anything at all
With no people or things in it
exs: The cookie jar was empty this morning.
Carlos held up an empty box.
The playground was empty after the rain.

defs: To come down to the ground after flying
To touch the ground after flying
To come down safely from the sky
exs: The helper robot will land on the roof.
Watch the bird land on the branch.
The plane will land in ten minutes.

defs: Having the most good things happen to you
More happy about good chances than anyone
Having more good surprises than anyone else
exs: Carlos felt like the luckiest boy in school.
She is the luckiest girl because she won the prize.
Mosh is the luckiest dog with so many toys.

defs: To tip a bottle so water comes out
To make milk or juice flow into a cup
To let liquid run out into something
exs: Carlos will pour milk into the bowl.
Please pour some juice for your sister.
Dad will pour tea into my cup.

defs: Filled so full that nothing else fits
Packed very tightly with things
Pushed full of things inside
exs: Carlos's bag was stuffed with snacks.
The toy box was stuffed full of teddy bears.
My pockets were stuffed with candy.

defs: A small bin for throwing away paper
A basket where you put trash
A basket by the desk for old things
exs: Carlos threw the torn paper into the wastebasket.
The wastebasket in my room is full.
Mosh tipped over the wastebasket.

defs: Hitting something by accident
Knocking into things again and again
Running into something with a small bang
exs: The robot kept bumping into the wall.
Stop bumping into your brother in the hall.
Carlos was bumping into chairs in the dark.

defs: Happy or sad things you have inside
What you have in your heart
Things like joy, fear and anger
exs: Carlos did not want to hurt his friend's feelings.
Mosh showed his feelings by wagging his tail.
It is okay to talk about your feelings.

defs: A thing with moving parts that does work
Something built to do a job faster
A thing that uses power to do work
exs: The washing machine is making a funny noise.
Carlos built a machine that sorts socks.
This machine makes ice cream.

defs: To throw things in many directions
To make things fly apart
To run away in different directions
exs: Carlos saw the birds scatter when the dog came.
Please don't scatter your toys on the floor.
The wind will scatter the leaves.

defs: Really wonderful and great
Very, very, very good
Great and so much fun
exs: We had a terrific day at the beach.
Carlos had a terrific idea for the science fair.
That is a terrific song!

defs: Spoke very softly so few could hear
Said something in a quiet voice
Talked quietly so others would not hear
exs: Carlos whispered a secret to Mosh.
She whispered during the quiet movie.
The girl whispered, "Be quiet, the baby is sleeping."

defs: A quick closing of one eye as a signal
Closing one eye fast to share a secret
A quick eye move that says it is a joke
exs: Dad gave me a wink when he told the joke.
Carlos gave his friend a wink and smiled.
With a wink, the robot said hello.

defs: At the back of something
On the other side, where you cannot see
After someone and not in front
exs: Mosh hid behind the big tree.
Carlos stood behind his mom in line.
The sun went behind the clouds.

defs: Running after someone to catch them
Going fast after something that runs away
Trying to catch something that is moving
exs: Mosh was chasing a butterfly in the yard.
The children were chasing each other at recess.
Carlos is chasing the ball down the hill.

defs: To say an answer when you are not sure
To try to give the right answer
To think something might be true
exs: Can you guess what is in the box?
I guess it will rain today.
Carlos could not guess the riddle.

defs: Done on purpose, not by accident
Meant to happen, not a mistake
Done in a way you planned
exs: Carlos did not break the cup intentionally.
She intentionally left the door open for Mosh.
He intentionally walked slowly to enjoy the view.

defs: The area around your home
The streets and houses close to where you live
A small part of a town where families live
exs: Carlos rode his bike around the neighborhood.
There is a new park in our neighborhood.
Everyone in the neighborhood knows Mosh.

defs: To move your head up and down to say yes
To move your head to show you agree
To bend your head down a little to say hello
exs: Carlos will nod when he understands.
The teacher saw me nod and smiled.
Please nod your head if you understand.

defs: Answered someone with words
Said something back after a question
Gave an answer when asked
exs: Carlos replied, "I'm fine, thank you."
She replied quickly to the teacher's question.
"I like it," Mom replied with a smile.

defs: To make someone jump from sudden surprise
To give someone a quick little fright
To surprise someone so they flinch
exs: A loud bang can startle the sleeping cat.
I did not mean to startle you.
Don't jump out and startle your sister.

defs: A thing that rings to wake you up
A machine by your bed that rings in the morning
Something you set so you wake up on time
exs: My alarm clock rings at seven every morning.
Carlos found an old alarm clock in the trash.
The alarm clock fell off the table.

defs: In a way that shows you are very mad
With a cross voice or face
In a mad and upset way
exs: Carlos stomped angrily into his room.
The man shouted angrily at the broken car.
She slammed the book down angrily.

defs: To be owned by someone
To be someone's own thing
To be kept by a person
exs: This toy does not belong to me.
Does this blue hat belong to you?
Those books belong to the library.

defs: The edge of the street next to the sidewalk
The hard edge along the side of a road
The place by the road for trash cans
exs: Carlos put the trash can by the curb.
Don't step off the curb without looking.
The car parked next to the curb.

defs: To pull something heavy along the ground
To tug something slowly behind you
To haul something that is hard to carry
exs: Carlos had to drag the heavy bag to the curb.
Mosh will drag his blanket everywhere.
Please don't drag your feet on the floor.

defs: Looked at something very carefully
Studied something closely to learn about it
Checked each part with great care
exs: Carlos examined the old clock closely.
The doctor examined my sore knee.
Mom examined the map to find the road.

defs: The reason a bad thing happened
Who is to blame for a problem
A mistake that someone is to blame for
exs: It was not Mosh's fault that the vase broke.
Carlos said, "It's my fault, I'm sorry."
Whose fault is the mess?

defs: Not special, just like all the others
Normal and not unusual
Common and plain, nothing strange about it
exs: It looked like an ordinary rock, but it glowed.
Today was an ordinary school day.
Carlos wore an ordinary gray jacket.

defs: Said no and would not do it
Would not take or accept something
Did not agree to do what was asked
exs: Mosh refused to eat his dinner.
Carlos refused the extra cake because he was full.
The little boy refused to go to bed.

defs: To give something back to its owner
To bring back something you borrowed
To take something back where it came from
exs: Carlos must return the book to the library.
Please return my pencil when you are done.
I will return the ball to my friend.

defs: Light shirts that girls and women wear
Tops with buttons for women
Pretty shirts that women wear
exs: Mom folded the blouses and put them away.
The shop sells blouses in many colors.
She washed two blouses on Sunday.

defs: Talked proudly about how great you are
Said you were better than others in a showy way
Boasted about something you did
exs: Carlos never bragged about winning the race.
The boy bragged about his new bike.
She bragged that she could jump the highest.

defs: A box you pull out of a desk
A sliding space for socks or papers
A part of a table you pull open
exs: Carlos put his socks in the top drawer.
The pencils are in the desk drawer.
Mosh opened the kitchen drawer with his nose.

defs: To think that something will probably happen
To wait for something because you believe it will come
To look forward to something you think is coming
exs: We expect rain on Saturday.
Carlos did not expect a gift from the robot.
I expect my friend to arrive soon.

defs: Very nice-looking and not plain
Decorated and special, not ordinary
Dressy and full of pretty details
exs: Carlos wore a fancy hat to the party.
The fancy cake had a sugar flower on top.
She bought fancy shoes for the dance.

defs: A look on your face when you are upset
A sad or cross look on your face
The face you make when you dislike something
exs: Dad had a frown when he saw the mess.
Carlos turned his frown into a smile.
There was a frown on Mosh's face.

defs: Confused, with things in the wrong places
Put together the wrong way so they are muddled
Not in the right order because of a mistake
exs: The socks got mixed up in the laundry.
Carlos was mixed up about which bus to take.
My papers got mixed up on the floor.

defs: A set of clothes worn together
What you choose to wear for a special day
Clothes that go well together
exs: Carlos picked a cool outfit for the party.
Her new outfit was red and yellow.
What outfit will you wear to school?

defs: Walked with loud, heavy steps because you were mad
Stepped hard on the floor to show you are upset
Walked noisily with heavy feet
exs: Carlos stomped up the stairs.
The little girl stomped her foot and said no.
The elephant stomped through the mud.

defs: to shine with small, quick flashes of light
what stars seem to do in the night sky
to sparkle on and off like a tiny light
exs: The stars twinkle high above our tent at night.
Her eyes twinkle when she tells a funny joke.
Lights twinkle on the tree in the living room.

defs: feeling like everything is spinning around you
feeling unsteady, as if you might fall over
how you feel after turning in circles many times
exs: I felt dizzy after spinning on the playground ride.
Carlos got dizzy when he stood up too fast.
The merry-go-round made Mosh feel very dizzy.

defs: in a soft, careful way
with very little force so nothing gets hurt
in a kind and soft manner
exs: Carlos gently pushed the swing for his little sister.
She gently patted the puppy on the head.
Please close the door gently so the baby can sleep.

defs: right away, with no waiting
at once, in a very short moment
so fast that there is no delay at all
exs: When the bell rang, the kids instantly ran outside.
The light came on instantly when I pressed the button.
Mosh instantly jumped up when he heard his name.

defs: in the place of something else
choosing one thing and not the other
used when one thing takes the place of another
exs: Let's walk to school instead of taking the bus.
He drank water instead of juice.
I read a book instead of watching TV.
